einzeiler: White House warns Democrats over Trump investigations, Biden discusses health and 2024…
kurzfassung: The White House cautioned congressional Democrats that aggressive plans to investigate President Trump's administration could cross legal boundaries into criminal conduct. Meanwhile, former President Joe Biden opened up about his cancer diagnosis and his disastrous 2024 debate performance in a new interview. In other news, authorities in South Carolina rescued an 11-month-old infant who was allegedly buried alive by his father.
stichpunkte: White House Counsel Will Scharf sent a letter warning Democrats that investigations driven by animus or harassment could be criminal.
Attorney Will Chamberlain noted that Democratic rhetoric makes it easier for the executive branch to argue subpoenas lack a legitimate legislative purpose.
Potential targets for congressional Democrats include cryptocurrency ventures, a Saudi investment in Jared Kushner's firm, and Pentagon contracts.
Former President Joe Biden stated in an interview that he would have resigned if he knew his fatigue was caused by aggressive prostate cancer.
Medical experts previously expressed skepticism that Biden's advanced cancer could have gone undetected during regular presidential checkups.
Biden downplayed his June 2024 debate against Trump, despite widespread Democratic alarm and Dr. Jill Biden fearing he was having a stroke.
An 11-month-old infant named Koa Sharp was rescued alive after being buried in a dog crate in the woods in South Carolina.
The infant's father, Michael Comer, was arrested and charged with attempted murder following a multi-agency search.
Former Wisconsin Lieutenant Governor Mandela Barnes filed a defamation lawsuit against the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel over a report on his relationships.

clips.hook: White House warns of blatant criminality
clips.text: The administration pushes back against aggressive oversight rhetoric, arguing that using investigations merely to intimidate opponents crosses legal boundaries.

clips.hook: Zero interest in running for second place
clips.text: The former lieutenant governor explains that fundraising difficulties and coalition building challenges led him to abandon his gubernatorial bid.

beschreibung:
The White House warns congressional Democrats that their planned investigations into President Trump's administration could cross legal boundaries, potentially setting up a series of courtroom battles - Will Chamberlain of the Article III Project weighs in. Former President Joe Biden says he would have resigned had he known about his cancer diagnosis while in office, and downplays his disastrous 2024 debate performance. South Carolina authorities rescue an 11-month-old baby who was allegedly buried alive by his father and left underground for nearly 24 hours. Former Wisconsin Lieutenant Governor Mandela Barnes sues the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel for defamation, alleging a reporter with whom he previously had a sexual relationship helped develop a damaging story about his involvement with other women.
